House Bill 449 By: Representatives Rhodes of The Senate Committee on Regulated Industries and Utilities offered the 124th, Ridley of the 6th, Hitchens of the 161st, Stephens of the 164th, Smith of the 70th, and others following substitute to HB 449: MOOT
A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT
To amend Title Titles 44 and 46 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to property and public utilities and public transportation, respectively, so as to subject prohibit certain restrictions on the installation, operation, or maintenance of private water wells for irrigation purposes on real property; to prohibit covenants running with the land from prohibiting or restricting property owners from installing, operating, or maintaining private water wells for irrigation purposes on their property; to prohibit companies providing that provide water services through certain water systems in this state to regulation by the Public Service Commission; from prohibiting or restricting customers of such company from installing, operating, or maintaining private water wells for irrigation purposes on such customers' property; to provide for the review of certain increases to the rates and charges of such companies by the commission; to provide for financial record keeping of such companies; to provide for rules and regulations; to provide for assessments and legislative recommendations by the commission; statutory construction; to provide for definitions; to provide an effective date; to provide for related matters; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.
BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF GEORGIA:
SECTION 1. Title 44 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to property, is amended in Article 3 of Chapter 5, relating to covenants and warranties, by adding a new Code section to read as follows: "44-5-60.1. (a) No covenant running with the land shall prohibit or restrict a property owner from installing, operating, or maintaining a water well on such property owner's property that exclusively provides water for irrigation purposes to such property, provided that such water well does not provide water to any other parcel of land that is not owned by such property owner and such property owner does not sell water from such water well or, in exchange for consideration, authorize the use of such water well by any other person. (b) Any provision in a covenant running with the land, or any subsidiary document adopted pursuant to a covenant running with the land, that violates subsection (a) of this Code section is declared to be contrary to public policy and shall be void and unenforceable. (c) It is the intent of the General Assembly that the provisions of this Code section shall apply to any covenant running with the land, or any subsidiary document adopted pursuant to a covenant running with the land, regardless of when such covenant running with the land was created or became effective. (d) Nothing in this Code section is intended to prevent the application of any provision of law or regulation of any county, municipality, or consolidated government concerning the installation, operation, or maintenance of water wells in this state." SECTION 2. Title 46 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to public utilities and public transportation, is amended by revising Chapter 10, which is reserved, as follows:
"CHAPTER 10
46-10-1. As used in this chapter, the term: (1) 'Covered water company' system' means any water system that is owned and operated by a private company and any affiliates or subsidiaries of such company that, collectively, provide that provides water services by means of pipes or conduits to 5,000 2,000 or more customer service connections in this state. Such term shall not include any water system that is owned or operated by the state or any political subdivision or authority thereof. (2) 'Surface water' means all rivers, streams, branches, creeks, ponds, tributary streams, drainage basins, natural lakes, and artificial reservoirs and impoundments. (3) 'Water services' means water services, waste-water sanitary sewer services, or both. (4) 'Water system' means a system for the provision to the public of piped water for human consumption that is sourced exclusively from surface water, sanitary sewer services, or both. Such term includes but is not limited to any collection, treatment, storage, and distribution facilities under the control of the operator of such system and used primarily in connection with such system and any collection or pretreatment storage facilities not under such control which are used primarily in connection with such system.
46-10-2. The rates and charges of covered water companies for water services shall be just and reasonable and shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the commission as provided in Code Section 46-10-3. 46-10-3. (b) Any contractual provision entered into by a company shall comply with the notice provisions of subsection (a) of said Code section prior to making such increase to its rates or charges. (b) If a hearing on the lawfulness of an increase to the rates or charges of that owns a covered water company for water services is held pursuant to system that violates the provisions of subsection (a) of this Code section and the commission determines at such hearing that such increase is just and reasonable, the commission shall not hold another hearing concerning an increase to the rates or charges of such covered water company for a period of three years, unless such covered water company intends to increase its rates or charges during such three-year period by 15 percent or more to the rates or charges found declared to be just contrary to public policy and reasonable by the commission at such hearing. (c) For purposes of calculating whether an increase to the rates or charges of a covered water company for water services constitutes an increase of 15 percent or more to the lowest amount such rates or charges have been set over the prior three calendar years, no one-time fees or charges assessed by such company for connecting to its water or sewer lines shall be included in such calculation. void and unenforceable.
46-10-4. A covered water company shall keep records relating to its financial condition and profits and losses in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. Such records shall be made available to (c) It is the commission upon request. 46-10-5. The commission Code section shall conduct regular assessments of its jurisdiction over apply to any contractual provision entered into by a company that owns a covered water companies as system regardless of when such contractual provision was entered into or otherwise became effective. 46-10-3. No company that owns a covered water system shall prohibit any customer of such company who receives water services from such company through such covered water system from installing, operating, or maintaining, or discontinue the provision of water services to such customer solely due to the installation, operation, or maintenance of, a water well on such customer's property that exclusively provides water for irrigation services to such customer; provided that such water well does not provide water to any parcel of land that is not owned by such customer and such customer does not sell water from such water well or, in exchange for consideration, authorize the use of such water well by another person. 46-10-4.
